thread:
nora: Heads up — customer ACME-42 reporting embeddings throughput collapse at ~11:15 UTC. Tokens/sec steady, vectors/sec dropped ~6x. They noticed latency spikes and 429-ish queueing. Can we triage?

liam: tagging @eng-oncall and @jun — any recent rollout that could affect batching/kvcoord? :eyes: 

ops-bot: [ALERT] svc=vecs-prod queue_depth > 1000 for 3m, p90 enqueue_latency 420ms, GPU utilization 98% on pool-g4. AlertID: alert-vecs-3949

eng-oncall: I'm on it. Nora — can you paste repro steps or a sample request that reproduces low vectors/sec? Also need a trace_id if available.

nora: quick repro from customer below — they send many small payloads (batch_size=1) at high qps. curl example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-42","input":["short text..."]}'
```
They reported this timing snapshot (client-observed): tokens/sec ~ 1.2k (unchanged), vectors/sec ~ 180/s (was ~1.1k/s).

jun: thanks — I'm seeing matching signals in infra: GPU kernels busy, but there are long waits in the KV coordination layer. Key log snippet from vec-router: 
```
2026-03-17T11:15:34Z WARN kvcoord: batch window shrink detected for model=open-embed-42, window_ms=2 -> 0 (rollout 57df1a)
2026-03-17T11:15:34Z INFO router: enqueue wait=312ms, queue_len=1123
2026-03-17T11:15:35Z ERROR batcher: dropped-batch due-to-no-slots count=17
```
Looks like a rollout changed the batch-window heuristic yesterday (rollout 57df1a). Could explain high enqueue wait and smaller effective batches.

liam: which release introduced that? link?

jun: PR https://git.redwood.internal/r/infra/kvcoord/pulls/1987 — small change to prefer latency-preferring windows for embeddings endpoints. The change landed in canary last week and rolled to prod in the 00:00 deploy.

nora: customer said the drop started at 11:15 — timeline aligns with autosplit/autoscaler reshard at 11:10. Could be interplay.

eng-oncall: quick experiment suggestion: flip the batching window back to previous value on one shard and run the customer's request pattern (batch_size=1 high qps) to compare vectors/sec. I can patch a single replica if we want a fast test.

sre-amy: FYI I observed a correlated increase in small-batch ratio: fraction_small_batches jumped from 12% -> 71% at 11:12. That amplifies KV lock contention.

jun: repro steps I ran against canary: python micro-repro snippet below (sends 2000 single-item requests at 500 qps):
```
# micro_repro.py
for i in range(2000):
  post('/v1/embeddings', payload=('short %d'%i))
  sleep(0.002)
```
Result: tokens/sec=1250, vectors/sec=190 (with rollout). Reverting the batch-window heuristic on that replica produced: tokens/sec=1260, vectors/sec=1020. So batching window change explains the vectors/sec regression.

liam: interesting — tokens/sec unchanged because tokenization & model forward still saturated, but vectors/sec dropped since we can't pack many requests into a batch -> GPU kernel overhead per batch.

billing-bot: Note: ACME-42 has high-volume account, no billing throttles applied. No invoice or quota anomalies found.

eng-oncall: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) rollback the batching-window heuristic rollout for embeddings models globally (safe, config-only), 2) apply a temporary rate-limiter to reduce enqueue storms (soft cap for small-batch ratio), 3) notify customer and open support SLA ticket. Which should we do now?

nora: customer is on a live sync job — they need recovery ASAP. Recommend rollback of rollout 57df1a for embeddings models and enable a small-batch autoscaler hack on the affected pool. Can you scope time?

jun: I can push a config rollback to prod in ~12 minutes and patch the autoscaler rule in ~20. I will also instrument per-model batch_size histograms for 48h.

eng-oncall: go for rollback first. Lets keep one shard on the new heuristic for live comparison. I'll also collect per-request traces (send trace id list). Nora — please send trace_id from customer.

nora: trace_id: tr-20260317-7a9b. Customer notified: "We identified a batching heuristic change that temporarily reduced vectors throughput; we're rolling back now and will update in ~30m." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: action=rollback config=kvcoord/heuristic/57df1a status=queued by=jun

ops-bot: action=rollback config=kvcoord/heuristic/57df1a status=applied shard=pool-g4-3 duration=42s

eng-oncall: initial post-rollback metrics: queue_depth dropped to ~120, p90 enqueue_latency 78ms, vectors/sec for customer sample back to ~980/s. Still watching for residual effects.

liam: can we add a regression alert for vectors/sec drop > 3x with tokens/sec stable? Might catch future heuristic regressions.

sre-amy: opened alert card A-vec-regress-3949 with threshold: vectors_rate < 40% baseline while tokens_rate in +-10%.

nora: Customer confirmed improvement on their side too. We'll monitor for 1h then close. Thanks all.

jun: follow-ups: add integration test that runs small-batch high-qps scenario in canary, and revert PR to include a gating flag for embeddings. I'll file follow-up PR.

nora: closing for now — will update thread if anything else pops up. :handshake:
